_comment: Built-in well-known TLS ClientHello fingerprints, shipped compiled-in via go:embed.
Users extend/override these by dropping JSON files (same schema, without this
_comment key) into ~/.traffic-deck/fingerprints/ (or $TRAFFICDECK_FP_DIR) — no rebuild.
Match keys, most specific first: 'ja4' (exact FoxIO JA4), 'ja4_pre' (a JA4 prefix,
e.g. the a_b sections = client+version era, stable while only the extension hash 'c'
changes across minor versions), 'ja4_b' (just the cipher-list hash = a whole client
family), 'ja3' (legacy MD5, exact). An optional 'sni' further constrains any row.
Keys may be COMBINED on one row, in which case all of them must match and the row
outranks a row constraining fewer keys — that's how to tell apart clients sharing a
JA4 but differing in JA3 (e.g. Chrome 133 vs a WebView): add a 'ja4'+'ja3' row per
variant and leave the bare 'ja4' row as the fallback for variants you haven't captured.
Later files win on ties, so a user row overrides a builtin.
PROVENANCE — every value below is real, not hand-typed:
* Exact per-version Chrome/Firefox/Safari/Edge JA4s were computed by this repo's own
ClientHello parser over ClientHellos generated by uTLS v1.8.2 (refraction-networking).
* Family/QUIC/unversioned rows are from FoxIO's ja4db mapping
(github.com/FoxIO-LLC/ja4, ja4plus-mapping.csv) and from local verified captures.
NOTE ON VERSIONS: JA4 is deliberately stable across browser versions — one JA4 spans
many releases (e.g. Chrome 120/121/.../131 all share _02713d6af862), and FoxIO's DB
itself does not version Chrome. So exact rows carry a version RANGE, and the cipher-
family rows (ja4_b) recognize any past/future version — including Chrome 139/144 — as
'Chrome' even when the exact era hash isn't listed. To pin a specific version you
haven't captured, capture it once and add its exact JA4 as a user row. Grow this file
from https://ja4db.com.

fingerprints.name: Chrome/Edge
fingerprints.note: Chromium 100-106 (Chrome/Edge share this), TLS/HTTP-2, SNI. uTLS-computed.

fingerprints.name: Chrome
fingerprints.note: Chrome 120-131 (FoxIO's canonical Chromium JA4). uTLS-computed + ja4db.

fingerprints.name: Chrome
fingerprints.note: Desktop Chrome 150 (Linux), HTTP/2, SNI. Verified capture.

fingerprints.name: Chrome
fingerprints.note: Desktop Chrome 150, HTTP/2, extra-extension variant. Verified capture.

fingerprints.name: Chrome (QUIC)
fingerprints.note: Chrome 150 over QUIC/HTTP-3, extension variant. Verified capture.

fingerprints.name: Chrome/Chromium
fingerprints.note: Any Chromium-based client over TLS/TCP (Chrome/Edge/Brave/Opera/Electron), any version incl. 139/144/future. Cipher-list family match; unique to Chromium in FoxIO ja4db.

fingerprints.name: Chrome/Chromium (QUIC)
fingerprints.note: Any Chromium-based client over QUIC/HTTP-3. Cipher-list family match.

fingerprints.name: Firefox
fingerprints.note: Desktop Firefox (SNI, HTTP-2), across versions. Prefix match on a_b; NOT a bare cipher-hash match, because Firefox and Android OkHttp share cipher hash 5b57614c22b0 and are told apart by the extension count in ja4_a (Firefox 15, OkHttp 10-13).

fingerprints.name: Firefox
fingerprints.note: Desktop Firefox without SNI (direct-IP). Prefix match. From FoxIO ja4db.

fingerprints.name: Safari / iOS
fingerprints.note: Apple Safari / iOS networking, any version. Cipher-list family match; unique to Apple in FoxIO ja4db.

fingerprints.name: Go net/http
fingerprints.note: Go standard-library crypto/tls client (net/http). Cipher-list family match. From FoxIO ja4db.

fingerprints.name: Python (urllib/requests)
fingerprints.note: Python stdlib ssl / requests / urllib3. Cipher-list family match. From FoxIO ja4db.
